prior_approach.content: Surface preparation methods for Nb SRF cavities include electropolishing, heat treatment, and high-pressure rinsing.
prior_approach.evidence_span: A variety of surface preparation techniques have been developed to improve RF performance. Electropolishing produces smoother surfaces, reducing local enhancement due to roughness, but introduces hydrogen absorption that must be removed by subsequent heat treatment. High-pressure rinsing with ultrapure water is then applied to remove microparticles and reduce field emission [1].

prior_approach.content: More recent prior methods include nitrogen doping/diffusion and low-temperature baking.
prior_approach.evidence_span: More recent advances include nitrogen doping and diffusion [2], as well as low-temperature baking [3, 4].

prior_approach.content: Thin-film cavities with superconducting coatings on bulk substrates have been developed.
prior_approach.evidence_span: This has motivated the development of thin-film cavities, in which a superconducting coating is deposited onto a bulk substrate.

prior_approach.content: An extension is SIS multilayer structures with insulating and superconducting thin layers on a bulk superconductor.
prior_approach.evidence_span: An extension of this concept is the use of superconductor-insulator-superconductor (SIS) multilayer structures [7]. Here, a bulk superconducting substrate is coated with a thin insulating layer O(10 nm) followed by a superconducting thin film O(100 nm) with higher 𝑇𝑐 and 𝐻𝑐.

prior_approach.content: Promising and related prior coating approaches include NbTiN-AlN-Nb multilayers, Nb3Sn/Nb bilayers, and Nb3Sn films on Cu.
prior_approach.evidence_span: One promising candidate is the NbTiN-AlN-Nb multilayer [9–11]. Other approaches include superconductor-superconductor bilayers, such as Nb3Sn on Nb produced via e.g. co-sputtering [12, 13], as well as Nb3Sn thin films on Cu substrates, expanding on the successes of Nb/Cu cavities [14].

prior_approach.content: These approaches rely on thin-film deposition methods such as ALD, co-sputtering, and DC magnetron sputtering, usually studied on flat samples.
prior_approach.evidence_span: All of these approaches rely on thin-film deposition techniques, e.g. atomic layer deposition, co-sputtering and DC magnetron sputtering, and are typically investigated on flat samples for quadrupole resonator (QPR) measurements [14, 15].

prior_approach.content: The study uses the finite element method to compute the cavity quality factor via an eigenvalue problem.
prior_approach.evidence_span: In order to obtain the quality factor of the cavity, we use the finite element (FE) method.

prior_approach.content: The Leontovich surface impedance boundary condition is adopted as the boundary treatment.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The latter, Eq. (2), is the Leontovich surface impedance boundary condition (SIBC) [16].

prior_approach.content: The surface-impedance model is based on the SIS multilayer treatment of Kubo et al.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The model by Kubo et al. [8, 20, 21] provides the magnetic fields under reasonable assumptions and simplifications for precisely this setup.

prior_approach.content: Gaussian random fields are used to model position-dependent coating thickness.
prior_approach.evidence_span: For this purpose, we use Gaussian random fields.

prior_approach.evidence_span: It is known that for zero-mean Gaussian random fields with Mat´ern covariance kernel, a sample can be generated by solving a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) [24].

prior_approach.evidence_span: Coating inhomogeneities were modeled using Gaussian random fields.

prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, such approaches remain fundamentally limited by the critical magnetic field of Nb (𝐻𝑐∼200 mT).

mechanism_principle.content: Only a thin surface layer matters because RF fields penetrate less than about 1 µm into superconductors.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Because RF fields penetrate only a very thin surface layer in superconductors (typically less than 1 µm [5]), the superconducting properties relevant for cavity performance are governed almost entirely by this thin layer.

mechanism_principle.content: Field decay at infinity means only the surface plane contributes to the surface integral in the Poynting-theorem derivation.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Since the fields must decay to zero at infinity, this means only the 𝑥 = 0 plane contributes to the surface integral.

mechanism_principle.content: Thickness variations determine the local surface impedance, which enters the boundary condition and thereby the eigenvalue problem.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This in turn defines 𝑍(𝒓, 𝜔), which is present in the boundary condition Eq. (2) and hence a component of the eigenvalue problem Eq. (9).

mechanism_principle.content: The maximum applicable field is controlled by layer thicknesses and bounded by the smaller of coating and substrate field limits through the gamma factors.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
This value depends on the layer thicknesses and is given by [8]

𝐵max = min {˜𝛾−1𝐵sh,NbTiN, 𝛾−1𝐵max,Nb}

mechanism_principle.content: If thickness parameters minimize surface resistance, the quality factor is maximized; deviations from that optimum can only preserve or reduce it, implying skewness.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Indeed, if one selects the thickness parameters to minimize the surface resistance, the highest quality factor would be reached. Deviating from this optimum would necessarily maintain or decrease the quality factor, yielding a very skewed distribution.

mechanism_principle.content: Different deposition methods are expected to produce different coating-thickness distributions.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Furthermore, one can expect the representative distributions to be quite different between e.g. sputtering based approaches such as co-sputtering [12, 13] and DC magnetron sputtering [14], or atomic layer deposition [10].

hypothesis_statement.content: The work proposes to numerically quantify how coating thickness variations affect TESLA-cavity quality factor.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In this work, we perform a numerical study to quantify the impact of coating thickness variations on the quality factor for a single cell TESLA cavity.

hypothesis_statement.content: The proposed simulation scheme is intended to apply broadly to thin-film approaches, with emphasis on SIS structures.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We outline a simulation scheme that is applicable to the mentioned thin-film approaches, though we focus on SIS structures in particular.

hypothesis_statement.content: The study expects different length scales of thickness variation to be meaningfully compared statistically.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Different length scales of the variations are considered and compared statistically.

evidence_result.content: Nb/Cu thin-film cavity implementation has been achieved at CERN facilities.
evidence_result.evidence_span: This approach has been successfully implemented in Nb/Cu cavities at CERN facilities such as LEP-II and LHC [6].

evidence_result.content: The derived resistive part matches the surface resistance reported earlier by Kubo's model.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We note that the resistive component of the surface impedance is identical to the surface resistance found in Ref. [8] through Joule dissipation.

evidence_result.content: Prior work reports dielectric-loss resistance as negligible relative to other contributions.
evidence_result.evidence_span: There, it is also mentioned that the resistance from dielectric losses is negligible compared to other contributions, concretely when 𝑑𝐼 = 100 nm, the contribution from dielectric losses is less than 10−5 nΩ, while the other contributions range from 10 nΩ to 1000 nΩ.

evidence_result.content: The illustrated samples show that the correlation length controls the spatial scale of thickness deviations.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We observe that, as the name suggests, 𝑙 controls the length scale over which deviations occur.

evidence_result.content: The optimal layer thicknesses for maximum applicable field are 10 nm insulator and 260 nm superconducting coating.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We find that the optimum is reached when 𝑑𝐼= 10 nm and 𝑑𝑆= 260 nm, hence these parameters will be used.

evidence_result.content: Q-Q plots indicate the quality factors are normally distributed for each length scale.
evidence_result.evidence_span: By observing Q-Q plots of the data, we observed that, in this case, the quality factors for each 𝑙 were normally distributed, i.e. 𝑄∼N (𝜇𝑄, 𝜎𝑄).

evidence_result.content: In extreme cases, inhomogeneous coating changes quality factor by about 6% relative to the uniform 260 nm coating.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In the most extreme cases, the quality factor deviates from that of a uniformly coated cavity with coating thickness 260 nm by approximately 6 %.

evidence_result.content: Standard-deviation error bars barely overlap across length scales, while mean error bars overlap substantially, especially at larger scales.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the error bars of the 𝜎𝑄 in Fig. 6 show barely any overlap, whereas the error bars of the 𝜇𝑄 overlap substantially, particularly for the larger length scales.

evidence_result.content: Mean quality factors for inhomogeneous coatings are consistently below the uniform-coating value.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We additionally observe that the 𝜇𝑄 of inhomogeneously coated cavities are consistently smaller than the uniform value, including the error bars.

evidence_result.content: Levene’s test shows the variances across the eight populations are not all equal.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The resulting 𝑝-value was extremely small, allowing rejection of the null hypothesis. Thus, the population variances are not all equal.

evidence_result.content: Pairwise Levene tests indicate all population variances are statistically distinct.
evidence_result.evidence_span: From the pairwise comparisons we conclude that all null hypotheses can be rejected. Hence, the variances of all populations are statistically distinct.

evidence_result.content: Welch’s ANOVA shows not all means are equal.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We find that the null hypothesis of equal means can be rejected with 𝑝= 4.8 × 10−5, indicating that not all means are equal.

evidence_result.content: Games-Howell post hoc testing finds most pairwise mean differences are not significant, with only a few weakly significant cases.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We find that the null hypothesis cannot be rejected in nearly all cases, and the few cases for which rejection is possible are only weakly significant.

evidence_result.content: Mean quality factors are mostly not statistically distinguishable, with only weak differences in a few cases.
evidence_result.evidence_span: From our analysis, we find that the 𝜇𝑄cannot be statistically distinguished in most cases, and only weakly so in a few instances.

evidence_result.content: All variances differ significantly, and increasing length scale mainly increases the spread of quality factor without significantly changing the mean.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In contrast, all variances differ significantly in the statistical sense. Hence, increasing 𝑙primarily results an increase in 𝜎𝑄, while no significant change in 𝜇𝑄is observed.

evidence_result.content: The uniform-coating quality factor is significantly above the confidence intervals of all inhomogeneous-coating means.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Nevertheless, we find that the quality factor corresponding to a uniform coating lies significantly above the confidence intervals of all 𝜇𝑄w.r.t the 95 % confidence interval.

evidence_result.content: Extreme observations show quality-factor changes of 2% to 6%, depending on length scale.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Depending on the length scale, extreme observations show a 2 % to 6 % increase or decrease in the quality factor.

evidence_result.content: Population means were mostly unchanged across length scales, with only weakly significant exceptions.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Our analysis revealed that the population means were mostly indifferent, with exceptions being only weakly significant

evidence_result.content: Standard deviations differed strongly across length scales.
evidence_result.evidence_span: however, pronounced differences were observed in the standard deviations.

evidence_result.content: The homogeneous-coating quality factor lies above the confidence intervals of all population means.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Furthermore, the quality factor of a homogeneous coating was found to lie above the confidence interval of all population means.

evidence_result.content: Extreme outcomes show the quality factor can increase or decrease by about 2% to 6% depending on length scale.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Finally, extreme observations indicate that, depending on the length scale, the quality factor may increase or decrease by approximately 2 % to 6 %.

mechanism_principle.content: Because RF fields penetrate only a very thin surface layer in superconductors (typically <1 µm), cavity performance is governed almost entirely by that layer; correspondingly, in the field-theoretic treatment the fields decay at infinity so the relevant surface contribution reduces to the surface plane in the Poynting-theorem derivation.
evidence_spans: Because RF fields penetrate only a very thin surface layer in superconductors (typically less than 1 µm [5]), the superconducting properties relevant for cavity performance are governed almost entirely by this thin layer.
Since the fields must decay to zero at infinity, this means only the 𝑥 = 0 plane contributes to the surface integral.

mechanism_principle.content: Thickness parameters set a surface-resistance optimum: choosing them to minimize surface resistance maximizes the quality factor, while deviations can only preserve or reduce the quality factor, leading to a skewed distribution of outcomes.

hypothesis_statement.content: The study proposes a numerical simulation scheme to quantify how coating thickness variations at different length scales affect the quality factor of a single-cell TESLA cavity, with statistical comparison across variation scales; the scheme is intended to be broadly applicable to thin-film approaches, with particular emphasis on SIS structures.
evidence_spans: In this work, we perform a numerical study to quantify the impact of coating thickness variations on the quality factor for a single cell TESLA cavity.
We outline a simulation scheme that is applicable to the mentioned thin-film approaches, though we focus on SIS structures in particular.
Different length scales of the variations are considered and compared statistically.

evidence_result.content: Mean quality factors for inhomogeneously coated cavities are consistently below the uniform/homogeneous-coating value, and the uniform-coating quality factor lies above the 95% confidence intervals of all inhomogeneous population means.

constraint.content: For the SIS design, the insulator and coating thicknesses are constrained to values that maximize the applicable magnetic field while maintaining the superconducting state.
